text:
maria: FYI customer 'BrightArc' is seeing repeating p95 spikes and intermittent 429s on their dedicated pool (eu2-dedicated-42). Started ~09:12 UTC, persists.
eli: Can you paste the API error pattern? 429 only or token errors too? :eyes: 
maria: Mostly 429 / throttling traces in the app logs, but we also see occasional token validation failures from our auth layer. Sample: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":3}`.
jason: Pool is dedicated but shared node slices (MIG) - possible neighbor saturation. Any recent packing changes?
luisa: I pulled scheduling logs for node eu2-node-119 at 09:10-09:20. Noticed repeated small bursts from tenant brightarc-proxy (bursting every ~6s). NVML shows SM % spike to 98% for ~200-400ms windows.
maria: Customer repro: small concurrent warm calls from many users. They claim they didn't change traffic.
eli: Upload the short nvtop snapshot and our per-tenant metrics (p50/p95 tokens). Also did autoscaler kick?
jason: Autoscaler didn't scale for that node - the pool-level autoscale metric used 30s windows and the bursts are too short to cross the threshold. We're only seeing avg GPU util ~45% despite high tail.
luisa: Here's a quick diagnostic snippet I ran on the node:
```
# nvml sample
Timestamp: 2026-03-12T09:13:02Z
SM Util: 97%, Mem Util: 42%
Process list: brightarc-proxy (slice 2) => sm-burst
```

eli: That explains 429s despite modest average util. This is classic noisy-neighbor microbursting on a shared node with MIG slices.
maria: Customer asked why autoscale didn't help — can we explain and offer mitigation?
jason: Short answer: autoscaler thresholds are averaged; small <1s bursts don't raise the aggregate signal. For dedicated pools with MIG slices, we should detect high tail SM occupancy and either throttle the offending tenant or offer rapid bump of capacity (burst slots).
luisa: Immediate remediation I recommend: 1) move brightarc to an isolated slice on a spare node if available, 2) enable temporary conservative rate cap for that tenant (soft limit), 3) schedule a pack rebalancing to avoid cohosting bursty inference workloads.
maria: Customer is OK with a temporary rate cap if we can minimize user impact.
eli: I'll push a mitigation plan:
- apply soft RPS cap (20% below observed median) for 15m
- if bursts continue, live-migrate tenant to spare isolated slice
- open a follow-up to runtime team for improved burst-detection metric (p95-sm-occupancy over 10s windows)
jason: Adding logs for the live-migrate command we used (internal):
```
# migrate tenant slice
rctl migrate --tenant brightarc --from-node eu2-node-119 --to-node eu2-standby-3 --mig-slice=isolated
```
luisa: After migration at 09:18, observed: SM spikes reduced to <30% and 429s subsided. Customer reported latency improved within 30s of migrate.
maria: Good. Any downstream follow-ups?
eli: Action items:
- Support: notify customer of mitigation + ask for any traffic pattern changes (maria)
- Runtime: add ad-hoc tail-sm metric and consider a short-window burst detector (luisa + eng-runtime)
- Autoscale: evaluate adding a burst-bump policy that reacts to sustained p95 spikes (jason + eng-sre)
- Billing: check if customer hit any overage during spike window (maria -> finance)
jason: I'll also add a postmortem note recommending we expose an API for reserved micro-burst tokens for dedicated customers.
maria: Customer update sent: "We've isolated the noisy workload and applied a temporary rate cap; we're monitoring and will follow up with a full report." :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident ticket #INC-20260312-784 created and linked to pool eu2-dedicated-42.
luisa: Quick data dump of p95 before/after (ms): `before: 420ms, after: 86ms`
eli: Nice. Let's keep the ticket open for the runtime follow-up and close when the new metrics/burst policy is in review.
maria: Thanks team — marking this as triaged. Will attach the nvml dumps and migration logs to the incident.
